\subsection{Matched-$K$ secondary mechanistic analysis}
This separately frozen secondary family holds $K=128$, claimed-label quotas, local steps, and the severe mixture fixed.  Audited clean shares are \IMDbMatchedRandomCleanPct\% for random-$K$, \IMDbMatchedRoutedCleanPct\% for routed-$K$, and \IMDbMatchedMaxPurityCleanPct\% for maximum-purity-$K$.  The routed-$K$ minus random-$K$ effect is \IMDbRoutedRandomDeltaPP\ pp (95\% CI [\IMDbRoutedRandomCILowPP, \IMDbRoutedRandomCIHighPP]; raw $p=\IMDbRoutedRandomRawP$, Holm $p=\IMDbRoutedRandomHolmP$).  The maximum-purity-$K$ minus routed-$K$ effect is \IMDbMaxPurityRoutedDeltaPP\ pp (95\% CI [\IMDbMaxPurityRoutedCILowPP, \IMDbMaxPurityRoutedCIHighPP]; raw $p=\IMDbMaxPurityRoutedRawP$, Holm $p=\IMDbMaxPurityRoutedHolmP$).  After Holm correction, routed-$K$ significantly outperforms random-$K$. Maximum-purity-$K$ does not show a statistically detectable gain over routed-$K$. These data therefore do not establish an additional accuracy gain from the higher audited clean fraction.  These are secondary mechanistic tests and do not confirm or replace the primary analysis.
